```{r}
#Install all packages before running
install.packages(c("here", "readr", "readxl", "data.table", "snafun", "igraph", "ergm"))
#dependencies = TRUE, force = TRUE)
```
## Data preparation

```{r load_data}
# Import all datasets
trade_data <- readxl::read_excel("trade_1988_2021.xlsx")
wb1 <- readxl::read_excel("P_Data_Extract_From_Doing_Business.xlsx")
wb2 <- readxl::read_excel("P_Data_Extract_From_World_Development_Indicators.xlsx")
wb3 <- readxl::read_excel("P_Data_Extract_From_Worldwide_Governance_Indicators.xlsx")

# Convert to data.table for manipulation
trade_data <- data.table::as.data.table(trade_data)
wb1 <- data.table::as.data.table(wb1)
wb2 <- data.table::as.data.table(wb2)
wb3 <- data.table::as.data.table(wb3)
```

```{r filter_trade}
# Select only 2018 observations with valid partners
trade_data_2018 <- trade_data[
  Year == 2018 &
    !ReporterName %in% c("Other Asia, nes", "World", "European Union") &
    !PartnerName %in% c("Other Asia, nes", "World", "European Union") &
    `TradeValue in 1000 USD` > 0
]
```

```{r clean_doing_business}
# Clean Doing Business data
wb1 <- data.table::setnames(wb1, old = names(wb1), new = make.names(names(wb1)))
wb1 <- wb1[, .(
  country_code = Country.Code,
  export_border_time_hrs = Time.to.export..Border.compliance..hours...DB16.20.methodology...TRD.ACRS.BRDR.EXPT.BRDR.COMP.HR.DB1619.,
  export_border_cost_usd = Trading.across.borders..Cost.to.export..Border.compliance..USD...DB16.20.methodology...TRD.ACRS.BRDR.EXPT.COST.BRDR.COMP.CD.DB1619.,
  export_doc_time_hrs = Time.to.export..Documentary.compliance..hours...DB16.20.methodology...TRD.ACRS.BRDR.DOC.COMP.HR.DB1619.,
  import_border_time_hrs = Time.to.import..Border.compliance..hours...DB16.20.methodology...TRD.ACRS.BRDR.IMP.BRDR.COMP.HR.DB1619.,
  import_border_cost_usd = Trading.across.borders..Cost.to.import..Border.compliance..USD...DB16.20.methodology...TRD.ACRS.BRDR.IMP.COST.BRDR.COMP.CD.DB1619.
)]
```

```{r clean_wdi}
# Clean macro indicators
wb2 <- data.table::setnames(wb2, old = names(wb2), new = make.names(names(wb2)))
wb2 <- wb2[, .(
  country_code = Country.Code,
  inflation_rate = Inflation..consumer.prices..annual.....FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.,
  gdp_growth = GDP.growth..annual.....NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.,
  gdp_current_usd = GDP..current.US....NY.GDP.MKTP.CD.
)]
```

```{r clean_wgi}
# Clean governance indicators
wb3 <- data.table::setnames(wb3, old = names(wb3), new = make.names(names(wb3)))
wb3 <- wb3[, .(
  country_code = Country.Code,
  gov_effectiveness = Government.Effectiveness..Estimate..GE.EST.,
  regulatory_quality = Regulatory.Quality..Estimate..RQ.EST.,
  control_corruption = Control.of.Corruption..Estimate..CC.EST.,
  rule_of_law = Rule.of.Law..Estimate..RL.EST.
)]
```

```{r merge_attributes}
# Merge attribute tables and keep countries observed in trade data
wb_combined <- merge(wb1, wb2, by = "country_code", all = FALSE)
wb_combined <- merge(wb_combined, wb3, by = "country_code", all = FALSE)
wb_combined <- unique(wb_combined, by = "country_code")

trade_countries <- unique(c(trade_data_2018$ReporterISO3, trade_data_2018$PartnerISO3))
wb_combined <- wb_combined[country_code %in% trade_countries]
dim(wb_combined)

```

```{r building_edges}
# Edge list with numeric weights is Export Value between 2 countries measured in 1000 USD
edge_list <- data.table::data.table(
  from = trade_data_2018$ReporterISO3,
  to = trade_data_2018$PartnerISO3,
  weight_raw = trade_data_2018$`TradeValue in 1000 USD`
)

# Use readr::parse_number to handle thousands separators from Excel correctly (2.796.481 -> 2796481)
edge_list[, weight_raw := as.character(weight_raw)]
edge_list[, weight_numeric := readr::parse_number(weight_raw)]

# Keep non-missing weights
edge_list <- edge_list[!is.na(weight_numeric) & weight_numeric > 0]

# Divide by 1000 to change units to Millions USD
edge_list[, weight_millions := weight_numeric / 1000]
print(edge_list)

#Summary statistics of edge weights
summary(edge_list$weight_millions)

# Plot the distribution of edge weights
log_trade_value  <- log1p(edge_list$weight_millions)


hist(
  log_trade_value,
  breaks = 100,
  main   = "Distribution of Trade Values (millions USD) log scale",
  xlab   = "Trade Value in millions USD log scale",
  col    = "blue"
)

```

```{r threshold}
#This huge gap mean most trade values are relatively small (around a few thousand), but a few very large trade relationships push the mean way up.
# Choose top 90% and cut below this threshold

threshold_90 <- quantile(edge_list$weight_millions, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
edge_list[, tie   := as.integer(weight_millions > threshold_90)]
print(edge_list)

# Quick density check for the selected threshold
nodes <- length(unique(c(edge_list$from, edge_list$to)))
possible_dyads <- nodes * (nodes - 1)
edges_90  <- sum(edge_list$tie)
density_90  <- edges_90  / possible_dyads
density_90

```


```{r building_vertices}
# Build vertex table (node attributes)
vertices <- data.table::copy(wb_combined)
data.table::setnames(vertices, "country_code", "name")

# Convert all non-name columns to numeric where possible
cols_to_numeric <- setdiff(names(vertices), "name")
vertices[, (cols_to_numeric) := lapply(.SD, readr::parse_number), .SDcols = cols_to_numeric]

# Countries that appear as either exporter (from) or importer (to)
edge_countries <- unique(c(edge_list$from, edge_list$to))

# Intersect with countries for which we have attributes
common_countries <- intersect(edge_countries, vertices$name)
length(common_countries)

# Keep only edges between countries that also have attributes
edge_list <- edge_list[from %in% common_countries & to %in% common_countries]

# Keep only vertices that actually appear in the (from/to) set
vertices <- vertices[name %in% common_countries]
print(edge_list)

```


```{r}
# Countries in edges
edge_countries <- unique(c(edge_list$from, edge_list$to))

# Countries with attributes
vertex_countries <- vertices$name

# Final set of countries in the network
countries <- sort(intersect(edge_countries, vertex_countries))

length(countries)  # just to see how many
```

```{r adjacency_matrix}
# Initialize matrix with zeros
trade_matrix <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = length(countries),
  ncol = length(countries),
  dimnames = list(countries, countries)  # row/col names
)

# Match from/to country codes to matrix row/col positions
row_idx <- match(edge_list$from, countries)
col_idx <- match(edge_list$to,   countries)

# Fill matrix: for each edge k, put weight_k at [from_k, to_k]
trade_matrix[cbind(row_idx, col_idx)] <- edge_list$tie
diag(trade_matrix) <- 0

dim(trade_matrix)
print(trade_matrix)
```


```{r}
# Next step is building a Data Frame of Node Covariates
# Countries in your matrix (must be the same as row/col names)
countries <- rownames(trade_matrix)

# 1. Take only these countries from vertices
analysis_vertices <- vertices[name %in% countries]

# 2. Reorder rows of analysis_vertices to match the matrix ordering
analysis_vertices <- analysis_vertices[match(countries, analysis_vertices$name)]
print(analysis_vertices)

# 3. Sanity check
stopifnot(identical(countries, analysis_vertices$name))
```

```{r}
# Scale border time and cost using analysis_vertices
log_border_time  <- log1p(analysis_vertices$export_border_time_hrs)
log_border_cost  <- log1p(analysis_vertices$export_border_cost_usd)

# Build covariate_data from analysis_vertices, using the scaled vectors
covariate_data <- data.frame(
  gdp_growth         = analysis_vertices$gdp_growth,
  regulatory_quality = analysis_vertices$regulatory_quality,
  rule_of_law        = analysis_vertices$rule_of_law,
  inflation_rate     = analysis_vertices$inflation_rate,
  log_border_time = as.numeric(log_border_time),
  log_border_cost = as.numeric(log_border_cost),
  row.names          = analysis_vertices$name
)

print(covariate_data)
str(covariate_data)

# Replace NA → 0.0 in numeric covariates
num_cols <- sapply(covariate_data, is.numeric)
# Logical matrix: TRUE where values are NOT finite (NA, NaN, Inf)
bad_mask <- !is.finite(num_cols)

covariate_data[, num_cols] <- lapply(covariate_data[, num_cols], function(x) {
  x[is.na(x)] <- 0
  return(x)
})

# Set inflation threshold is 30 and replace inflation > threshold with 0.0 to avoid outlier
threshold = 30
covariate_data$inflation_rate[covariate_data$inflation_rate > threshold] <- 0
print(covariate_data)
stopifnot(!any(!is.finite(as.matrix(covariate_data[, num_cols, drop = FALSE]))))
stopifnot(!any(!is.finite(trade_matrix)))

```

```{r Creating_trade_network}
# Create a network from trade_matrix

trade_network <- network::network(trade_matrix, 
                                  matrix.type = "adjacency", 
                                  directed = TRUE, 
                                  hyper = FALSE, 
                                  loops = FALSE, 
                                  multiple = FALSE, 
                                  bipartite = FALSE, 
                                  ignore.eval = TRUE, 
                                  names.eval = NULL, 
                                  na.rm = FALSE, 
                                  edge.check = FALSE)


trade_network

# Make sure ordering matches
stopifnot(identical(
  network::get.vertex.attribute(trade_network, "vertex.names"),
  rownames(covariate_data)
))
covariate_clean <- data.frame(
  gdp_growth        = as.numeric(covariate_data$gdp_growth),
  regulatory_quality = as.numeric(covariate_data$regulatory_quality),
  rule_of_law        = as.numeric(covariate_data$rule_of_law),
  inflation_rate     = as.numeric(covariate_data$inflation_rate),
  log_border_time    = as.numeric(covariate_data$log_border_time),
  log_border_cost    = as.numeric(covariate_data$log_border_cost),
  row.names          = rownames(covariate_data)
)


# Now attach each attribute one by one
for (attr_name in colnames(covariate_clean)) {
  vals <- covariate_clean[[attr_name]]
  vals <- as.vector(vals)  # ensure it's a plain vector

  network::set.vertex.attribute(
    trade_network,
    attrname = attr_name,
    value    = vals
  )
}

network::list.vertex.attributes(trade_network)
```

```{r}
imports_dt <- edge_list[, .(

), by = to]

head(imports_dt)
vnames <- network::get.vertex.attribute(trade_network, "vertex.names")

imports_full <- data.table::data.table(name = vnames)

# Merge totals by country code (to)
imports_full <- imports_dt[imports_full, on = .(to = name)]

# Countries with no imports in your data will have NA -> set to 0
imports_full[is.na(total_imports), total_imports := 0]

imports_full[, log_total_imports := log1p(total_imports)]

# Log transformation
imports_full

network::set.vertex.attribute(
  trade_network,
  "log_total_imports",
  imports_full$log_total_imports
)
trade_network

```

```{r Build baseline model}
set.seed(342)
mod_baseline <- ergm::ergm(trade_network ~ edges + 
                     absdiff("regulatory_quality") + 
                     absdiff("rule_of_law") +
                     nodeicov("log_total_imports") +
                     nodecov("gdp_growth"))


summary(mod_baseline)

```


```{r Build more complicated model - Dyadic dependence}
set.seed(342)
mod <- ergm::ergm(trade_network ~ edges + 
                     absdiff("regulatory_quality") + 
                     absdiff("rule_of_law") +
                     nodeicov("log_total_imports") +
                     nodecov("gdp_growth") +
                     mutual,
                    control = ergm::control.ergm(MCMC.burnin = 6000,
                                              MCMC.samplesize = 30000,
                                              seed = 342,
                                              parallel = 4,
                                              MCMLE.MCMC.precision = 0.05,
                                              MCMLE.maxit = 30))



summary(mod)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
ergm::mcmc.diagnostics(mod)

```


```{r Build more complicated ERGM models - Dyadic Dependent}
set.seed(342)
mod1 <- ergm::ergm(trade_network ~ edges + 
                     absdiff("regulatory_quality") + 
                     absdiff("rule_of_law") +
                     nodeicov("log_total_imports") +
                     nodecov("gdp_growth") +
                     mutual + 
                     dgwesp(decay = 0.15, fixed =TRUE, type="OTP") +
                     gwidegree(0.15, fixed = TRUE) +
                     dgwdsp(decay = 0.15, fixed =TRUE, type="OTP"),
                    control = ergm::control.ergm(MCMC.burnin = 6000,
                                              MCMC.samplesize = 50000,
                                              seed = 342,
                                              parallel = 4,
                                              MCMLE.MCMC.precision = 0.05,
                                              MCMLE.maxit = 45))
summary(mod1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
ergm::mcmc.diagnostics(mod1)


fit.mod1 <- ergm::gof(mod1)
snafun::stat_plot_gof(fit.mod1)

```



```{r}
set.seed(342)
mod3 <- ergm::ergm(trade_network ~ edges +
```
